faq.q: How much does April Injury Law charge?
faq.a: April Injury Law publishes a contingency fee, which means the fee is a share of what the case recovers and there is nothing to pay if it recovers nothing. The rate itself is not published, so ask for it in writing, along with how case expenses are handled and whether they come out of the recovery before or after the fee. The first consultation is free, which is the place to ask.

faq.q: Does April Injury Law offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. April Injury Law publishes a free initial consultation. The intake line is published as open around the clock.

faq.q: Where does April Injury Law have offices?
faq.a: April Injury Law publishes one office, in Las Vegas. Addresses and the Google listing behind each one are on this profile under Offices.

faq.q: Who are the attorneys at April Injury Law?
faq.a: April Injury Law names no attorney on the public pages we could read. That is a gap in what the firm publishes rather than a statement about who works there, and it is why the licensure and discipline checks on this profile have nothing to run against.

faq.q: Are the case results April Injury Law publishes verified?
faq.a: No. April Injury Law publishes 23 case results with amounts on its own site. We counted them and we did not confirm them: the figures are the firm's. Pillar B scores whether a firm publishes outcomes and discloses them properly, including whether a prior-results disclaimer appears beside them, not whether the amounts are right. Past results do not predict another case.
